alpha10ColonContextRepair.rule: After a bare colon, a value that looks like a type or like code is kept only with independently recognisable source context in the engine's bounded view (at most 512 bytes before the key, in the same text or JSON string). For a type: a fn signature, a struct, interface or type body around the key, or a let/const/var declaration naming it. For code: one of those, an object literal that is assigned or passed to json!, or a labelled argument of an unclosed call whose ( directly follows a callee. A source-shaped value does not establish context. Without context the value is credential data and redacts. The rule holds for every credential key, not only the password nouns. docs/SPEC.md states it.

blockingClasses.class: context-free generic-type exemption after a colon
blockingClasses.fix: A balanced angle-bracket string, a simple type word or a borrowed type after a bare colon is a type only with source context; otherwise it redacts, as it already did after = and "is". A comma or semicolon does not make a value a type.
The controls that pinned a context-free type after a colon moved to the positive sets, as the ruling asked.

blockingClasses.class: context-free code-looking values (same class, found while repairing)
blockingClasses.fix: A match expression, call, member chain, arrow function, function() {…}, ?? or || fallback, or & borrow after a bare colon had the same context-free exemption. It now needs source context too, for every credential key.
